Generate a Synthetic CSV From a Schema Recipe

Source: R/lib_synthetic.R
make_synthetic_csv.Rd

Generates a reproducible synthetic data set from a recipe (the schema$synthetic_recipe block of a provenance object, or a list written by hand) and writes it to a CSV file. Each column is described as in make_synthetic_column. Next to the CSV it writes a .synthetic marker file, so the generated rows can never be mistaken for real data later. Use it to share a runnable version of an analysis without sharing restricted records.

Usage

make_synthetic_csv(schema, out_path, n_rows = NULL, seed = NULL)

Arguments

schema

The synthetic recipe: a list with columns (a named list of column specs), and optional n_rows, seed and row_replication.

out_path

Character string: the path of the CSV to write.

n_rows

Whole number: the number of rows (persons, if replicating) to generate. Defaults to schema$n_rows, then 50000.

seed

Random seed for reproducibility. Defaults to schema$seed, then 91735246.

Value

Invisibly, an object of class bricklayer_synthetic: a list with path, sidecar (the <path>.synthetic marker file; verify_capsule treats its presence as a failed check), rows (rows written), seed (the seed used) and recipe_sha256 (the recipe's digest, NA when it could not be computed). Its print method labels the file as synthetic.

Details

Columns are produced in declaration order so later columns can reference earlier ones. A shared per-person latent propensity, uniform on \([0, 1]\), drives every "bernoulli" column through its p_with_baserate field, so those columns are correlated with each other. An optional row_replication block (values and weights) draws how many rows each person gets: person-level columns are drawn once per person and repeated, while "bernoulli" columns are drawn once per row. With replication the file therefore has more than n_rows rows.

The data are drawn under seed and the caller's random number stream is restored afterwards, so the same recipe and seed give the same file and the surrounding analysis is not disturbed.

Side effects: writes out_path (overwriting it) and paste0(out_path, ".synthetic"), a small JSON file with synthetic: true, the row count, the seed, the recipe's SHA-256 and the time; and marks the R session as having made synthetic data, so a manifest built later in the same session is labelled synthetic. A progress bar is shown in an interactive session.

Errors: schema not a list; any error from make_synthetic_column; an unwritable out_path.

See also

make_synthetic_column, verify_capsule.

Examples

recipe <- list(
  n_rows = 20, seed = 42,
  columns = list(
    year   = list(type = "sample", values = list(2024, 2025)),
    alert  = list(type = "bernoulli", p = 0.2),
    visits = list(type = "poisson", lambda = 3, min = 1),
    id     = list(type = "id_pattern", pattern = "p-{seq:05d}")
  )
)
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
res <- make_synthetic_csv(recipe, out)
res$rows # 20
#> [1] 20
res$seed # 42 (reproducible)
#> [1] 42

# The written CSV round-trips and has the declared columns.
df <- utils::read.csv(out)
dim(df)
#> [1] 20  4
names(df)
#> [1] "year"   "alert"  "visits" "id"    

# and the marker file says it is synthetic
file.exists(res$sidecar)
#> [1] TRUE

# n_rows overrides the recipe's own row count.
make_synthetic_csv(recipe, tempfile(fileext = ".csv"), n_rows = 5)$rows
#> [1] 5

# one to three rows per person
recipe$row_replication <- list(values = list(1, 2, 3))
make_synthetic_csv(recipe, tempfile(fileext = ".csv"), n_rows = 5)$rows
#> [1] 6

try(make_synthetic_csv("not a recipe", tempfile()))
#> Error : `schema` must be a schema list (columns = ..., ...)
